asr.languageHintMobile: Applies to on-device recognition and Alibaba Cloud paraformer-v2 / fun-asr; Volcengine and Qwen ASR auto-detect
asr.languageHintDesktop: Applies to on-device recognition and Alibaba Cloud paraformer-v2 / fun-asr; Volcengine and Qwen ASR auto-detect
asr.concurrencyHint: Subtitle batches sent to LLM for correction in parallel; higher is faster but limited by model concurrency (DeepSeek-flash 2500 / pro 500, recommended 5–16 for regular endpoints).
asr.importCorrectionHint: After importing Bilibili subtitles, run LLM correction for typos, punctuation, and math formulas (same as ASR transcripts). Disable to use subtitles as-is.
asr.localModelHintMobile: SenseVoice is recommended on phones: a 240 MB model that uses about 350 MB of RAM and transcribes an hour-long lecture in minutes, offline and free. Qwen3-ASR is more accurate but needs about 2.5 GB of RAM — only use it on an iPad with plenty of memory.
asr.localModelHint: SenseVoice is fast and accurate for Chinese lectures. Qwen3-ASR is a bit more accurate and also handles English and 30+ other languages, so use it for English or heavily mixed lectures. On the CPU it is 2–3× slower than SenseVoice; turn on GPU acceleration to speed it up. The 1.7B model makes about a sixth fewer errors than 0.6B but is twice as slow and a 2.5 GB download; use it with a dedicated GPU or Apple silicon. If the chosen model isn't downloaded, another downloaded model is used.
asr.localHotwordsHint: Qwen3-ASR favors these terms (shared with Volcengine). Only list terms the lectures actually use — words that never come up may get forced into the transcript.
asr.hotwordsHint: One per line (or comma-separated), max 5000; proper nouns, names, terms
asr.hotwordsPlaceholder:
Le Chatelier's principle
Enthalpy
Van der Waals force
asr.contextHint: Video title and course name are auto-included; add accent/domain/scene hints here (~800 tokens max, one per line)
asr.contextPlaceholder:
This is a high school chemistry reaction kinetics course
The instructor has a regional accent
asr.gpuHint: Transcribe on the graphics card, 2–3× faster: on Windows any NVIDIA, AMD or Intel GPU works (no CUDA install needed); on Mac it uses Apple silicon. Falls back to the CPU when no usable GPU is found; the progress text shows which device was used.

llm.title: LLM
llm.autoGenerateHint: Which items the model generates on its own once a video finishes processing. Switched-off items send no request and cost nothing; they show as skipped in the progress view, and you can still generate them from their panel.

ocr.title: OCR
ocr.paddleModelHint: PP-OCRv6 reads Chinese slides more accurately than the system OCR, fully offline. Stored alongside the speech recognition models.
ocr.paddleDeleteConfirm: Delete the PaddleOCR model? Slide OCR will switch back to the on-device OCR; you'll need to download it again to use it.
ocr.aliyunSecretHint: Leave empty to keep the saved secret. Enable “OCR” in the Alibaba Cloud console first.
ocr.deepseekKeyHint: Leave empty to keep the saved key. Create an API key on the DeepSeek platform and enable a vision model first.

semantic.sourceHint: Finds relevant passages even when your wording differs from the lecture's. Used by course search, course Q&A and the AI assistant. Keyword search is always on; this adds to it. Vectors are computed on this device or by the endpoint you choose, and stored only on this device.
semantic.localUnsupported: On-device models aren't available on phones. Use a cloud endpoint instead.
semantic.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}"? Existing indexes are kept and work again if you re-download the same model.
semantic.noProfiles: No usable endpoint yet. Add an OpenAI-compatible (or Azure) profile under LLM first. DeepSeek and Anthropic have no embeddings API, so add a separate Qwen, SiliconFlow or OpenAI profile for vectors.
semantic.cloudProfileHint: Calls this profile's /embeddings endpoint with its address and key. Only OpenAI-compatible and Azure profiles are listed.
semantic.cloudModelHint: A model made for embeddings, not a chat model: text-embedding-v4 for Qwen / Bailian, text-embedding-3-small for OpenAI, BAAI/bge-m3 on SiliconFlow. Changing it rebuilds the index with the new model.
semantic.indexHint: Each video's transcript is embedded once and stored on this device. Newly processed videos and edited transcripts are picked up in the background; videos not indexed yet still use keyword search.
semantic.inactive: Not ready yet: download the on-device model, or pick a profile and enter a model name.
semantic.rebuildConfirm: Delete every index for the current model and rebuild from scratch? This takes a while with many videos, and a cloud endpoint will bill again.

lanShare.hint: On the same Wi‑Fi, a phone or another computer opening a video it has no file for streams it straight from this computer: nothing is uploaded to the drive and nothing takes up space on the phone. Devices connected to the same drive find this computer automatically, with no pairing code. The connection is encrypted and only trusts this computer's certificate. CoursePilot needs to be running here; the first time on Windows you'll be asked to allow network access — allow it on private networks.
lanShare.toggle: Let devices on the same Wi‑Fi play videos stored on this computer
lanShare.noNetwork: On, but not connected to a network right now
lanShare.mobileHint: Turn on "Play over local network" under Settings → Sync on your computer. Then, when this device is on the same Wi‑Fi, videos whose files are only on the computer play straight from it without downloading.

remoteSync.connectionHint: Sync your study data between computer and phone through your own WebDAV drive. Use the same drive and folder on every device. Synced: courses and folders, video entries, notes (with images), clips, review cards, study history, playback progress, plus transcripts and AI-generated content (chapters, summaries, quizzes, mind maps, highlights, concepts). Video files have their own switch below.

urlHint.jianguoyun: Jianguoyun's WebDAV address is always https://dav.jianguoyun.com/dav/.
urlHint.nextcloud: Nextcloud shows it under Files → Settings, like https://your-server/remote.php/dav/files/username/.
urlHint.custom: The WebDAV address from your service (starting with http:// or https://).

remoteSync.passwordHintJianguoyun: Jianguoyun needs an app password: web → Account → Security → Third-party apps → Add. Not your login password.
remoteSync.folderHint: Sync data lives in this folder; use the same one on every device. Created if missing.
remoteSync.testOk: Connected · {{count}} device(s) already on the drive
remoteSync.syncHint: Once on, syncs automatically: changes made here usually go up within a minute or two. Changes from other devices come down within minutes while you are active, slowing to every 30 minutes when nothing has changed for a while, and right away whenever the app comes back to the foreground. The first sync uploads everything already on this device, which can take a few rounds.
remoteSync.needConfig: Fill in and save the drive first
remoteSync.noDevices: No other devices on the drive yet. Enter the same drive and folder in CoursePilot on another device and turn sync on.
remoteSync.retireConfirm:
"{{name}}" will no longer appear in the device list, and its old sync records on the drive will be merged into one to free up space. Notes, progress and other data it wrote are kept, and new devices still receive them.

Use this for an old phone you no longer use, or records left over from before a reinstall. If that device is actually still in use, it reappears the next time it syncs.
remoteSync.uploadMediaHint: Uploads this device's videos to the drive in 64 MB pieces so other devices can download them. Videos are big: Jianguoyun's free plan allows only 1 GB of uploads a month (42 GB on Pro); for whole courses, Nextcloud, Synology or a large drive mounted via Alist works better. Turn this on only on the device that has the videos.
remoteSync.uploadIdle: Files already on the drive aren't re-uploaded; interrupted uploads resume from the missing piece

webdavImport.title: Import from a cloud drive
webdavImport.intro: Connect a drive first. Jianguoyun, Nextcloud and Synology connect directly, and Quark Drive needs a cookie from its website; for Baidu Netdisk, Aliyun Drive or 115, expose them as WebDAV with OpenList first.

presetHints.openlist: OpenList exposes Baidu, Aliyun, Quark, 115 and more as one WebDAV address (http://computer-ip:5244/dav/ by default); use your OpenList account. First time? Follow the steps below.
presetHints.jianguoyun: Use an app password (Jianguoyun web → Account → Security), not your login password.
presetHints.nextcloud: Find the address in Nextcloud web → Files → Settings (bottom left).
presetHints.synology: Install WebDAV Server from Package Center and enable HTTPS; the address is usually https://your-nas:5006/.
presetHints.other: Enter the drive's WebDAV address, user name and password.
presetHints.quark: Quark has no developer platform, so this uses your web login: sign in at pan.quark.cn → F12 → Network → reload, click any request and copy the whole Cookie header. It expires after a while; non-members are speed-limited.

openlistGuide.title: How to mount Baidu Netdisk with OpenList (5 steps, once)
openlistGuide.install: Download and install OpenList Desktop (Windows and Mac) on your computer. On first launch, follow the guide to install the OpenList service, open the admin page at http://127.0.0.1:5244 and note the admin user name and password.
openlistGuide.storage: Admin page → Storages → Add → choose "Baidu Netdisk". To get the refresh token: open the address below, choose Baidu Netdisk, tick using OpenList's parameters, sign in to Baidu, paste the token back, and turn on "use online api" in the storage.
openlistGuide.policy: In the same storage, set "WebDAV policy" to "Local proxy" (most compatible; large files aren't blocked by Baidu). Any mount path works, e.g. /Baidu.
openlistGuide.permission: Admin page → Users → edit admin → tick "WebDAV read" under permissions.
openlistGuide.connect: Back here, use http://127.0.0.1:5244/dav/ as the address (on a phone, use the computer's LAN IP, e.g. http://192.168.1.5:5244/dav/), with your OpenList user name and password. When watching on a phone, the computer must be running OpenList on the same Wi‑Fi.
openlistGuide.others: Aliyun Drive, 115 and Tianyi Cloud work the same way — pick that storage type in step 2.

settings.title: First, set up an LLM and speech recognition
settings.body: Speech recognition turns lectures into transcripts; the LLM writes notes, quizzes and answers. Click Next and we’ll walk you through Settings.

llm.title: LLM — DeepSeek as an example
llm.body: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and Azure all work; pick a preset to fill in the protocol and endpoint, then fetch the model list.
llm.step1: Sign up on the <link>DeepSeek Platform</link> and create an API key (top up if your balance is low)
llm.step2: Pick the DeepSeek preset on the left and click Add; the Base URL is filled in as https://api.deepseek.com
llm.step3: Enter the API key, click Fetch models and pick one (context and reference pricing are shown), then Save

asr.title: Speech recognition — Volcengine or Alibaba Cloud
asr.body: Without it, on-device recognition is used (download SenseVoice for Chinese lectures). Cloud recognition doesn't use your computer's resources, and phones can only use the cloud.
asr.bodyMobile: Without it, pick "On-device" under Speech recognition and download SenseVoice (240 MB, works offline). Cloud recognition saves your phone's battery.
asr.volc: Volcengine: enable <link>Recording File Recognition (LLM)</link> to get an App ID and Access Token; set ASR backend to “Volcengine file transcription”, fill them in and click “Save Volcengine ASR credentials”
asr.aliyun: Alibaba Cloud: enable speech recognition in the Bailian console and create an API key (starts with sk-); set ASR backend to “Alibaba Cloud DashScope file transcription”, paste the key and click “Save Bailian API Key”

addCourse.title: Finally, create a course and import videos
addCourse.step1: Click “New Course Folder” and pick the folder that holds your lecture videos — they’re imported automatically
addCourse.step2: Inside a course, Import also takes local videos or Bilibili / YouTube links (the first Bilibili download asks for cookies.txt)
addCourse.step2Mobile: Inside a course, Import lets you pick videos from Photos or Files
addCourse.step3: Videos are transcribed, slides captured and notes written automatically — follow along in the processing queue

import.title: Bring in your videos
import.body: Upload local video or audio, or paste a Bilibili / YouTube link. Imports are transcribed and slides are captured automatically; with an LLM they become notes too.

findExplain.title: Snap a problem, find where it’s taught
findExplain.body: Snap a photo, paste a screenshot, or type the problem — it searches this course’s transcript and slides for where it’s explained, and can play those clips in order. Pasting an image on the course page works too.

concepts.title: Knowledge: this course’s concept map
concepts.body: Every concept pulled from the videos, with an explanation and where it’s taught; each one can be explained back with “Explain it to me” and gets a check once you do.

tabs.title: Your study materials live here
tabs.body: Once processing finishes, the overview, transcript and notes appear here; quizzes, slides and mind maps are under More.

notes.title: Press {{key}} to take a note
notes.body: The video pauses and the current timestamp is added at your cursor. Change the key in Settings → Shortcuts.

transcript.title: Select a line in the transcript
transcript.body: Highlight any text to ask AI about it, quote it to your notes, or make a cloze card.

assistant.title: Stuck? Ask the AI assistant
assistant.body: Click here (or press {{key}}). It has read this course’s transcript and slides, and timestamps in its answers are clickable. Turn on “Guide” and it won’t hand you the answer — it asks you step by step. Selecting a transcript line and choosing “Guide me through this” works too.
assistant.bodyTouch: Tap here. It has read this course’s transcript and slides, and timestamps in its answers are clickable. Turn on “Guide” and it won’t hand you the answer — it asks you step by step.

feynman.title: Explain it to find the gaps
feynman.body: In the Key chapters header, “Feynman explanation” lets you pick a chapter and explain it in your own words (speak or type). The AI checks only against the course text, shows what you missed or got wrong, and links back to the exact moment. You'll also get a gentle nudge when a chapter ends.

highlights.title: Speed up or skip the filler
highlights.body: Open Highlights in the player settings: the AI marks admin talk, chit-chat and repeated explanations. Speed them up or skip them, see how many minutes it saves, and undo anything it gets wrong.
highlights.bodyTouch: Tap the video to show the controls, then open Highlights in the settings: the AI marks admin talk, chit-chat and repeated explanations — speed them up or skip them, and it shows how many minutes it saves.

focus.title: Need to concentrate?
focus.body: Focus reading lets the study panel fill the workbench with the text centered while the video keeps playing. Press Esc to leave.

notesTouch.title: Jot a note as you watch
notesTouch.body: Tap Take a note in your notes: the video pauses and the current timestamp is added. With a keyboard, just press {{key}}.
